gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-sarala: Marker-bold, wide-mouthed and playful: Shantell Sans. Sarala is a friendly sans with open gaps in its rounded letters and a stroke like neon tubing, so paragraphs keep moving smoothly down the page.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-zcool-xiaowei: Rope-thick strokes and a wide-mouthed grin: Shantell Sans. ZCOOL XiaoWei sits beneath with a gentle taper, like a sharpened pencil line, so the rope-like heading and the finer body feel deliberately unlike.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-mukta-malar: Expressive and stencil-cut, Snowburst One stands tall with wide gaps between letters. Its sharpest trait is the gap in scale, since Mukta Malar, a sans-serif with compressed ascenders, stays modest beside the tall display lowercase.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-yantramanav: Stencil-cut and tall, Snowburst One makes a loud entrance with wide bridges. And Yantramanav, a sans whose huddled lowercase nearly reaches capital height, gives the loud heading something dense to push against.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-display: Tube-bright and splayed, Tilt Neon draws every stroke at constant width, topped with short ascenders over a large x-height. Noto Sans Display lets its own tall middle zone do the talking.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-hanken-grotesk: Round, open-parenthesis forms in a pen-like line: Turret Road. Hanken Grotesk, a plain sans with a wire-bent look and wide channels into every counter, supplies all the restraint that bold heading lacks.
gen-gf-underdog-gf-noto-sans-inscription: Noto Sans Inscriptional Pahlavi keeps small counters clear and unclogged. Underdog, whose lines bend like a straw with a horseshoe-wide c, is the loud half, and that gap in temperament is the draw.
